Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` for correctness.

findings.title: Category fabricators were deleted from category_fabricator.rb and moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, breaking the fabricator file naming convention
findings.body: The diff shows all four category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were removed from `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` (leaving it containing only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator) and re-added verbatim into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Two problems: (1) `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` — a file named after categories contains an unrelated fabricator, and the embeddable host fabricator is defined in two places conceptually (the file `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains only category fabricators, so its name is wrong too). (2) More concretely, Fabrication loads fabricator files by convention; having the `:embeddable_host` fabricator in `category_fabricator.rb` and the category fabricators in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` is confusing and error-prone — if any tooling or future refactor deletes 'unused' fabricator files by name, all category fabricators (used by hundreds of specs, e.g. spec/models/topic_spec.rb) would vanish. The `:embeddable_host` fabricator belongs in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` and the category fabricators belong in `category_fabricator.rb`.

findings.title: Authorization relies on redundant before_filter instead of AdminConstraint used by sibling admin controllers
findings.body: The controller declares `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` while the routes already wrap `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` (config/routes.rb:153). `ensure_staff` allows moderators, whereas `AdminConstraint` restricts to admins — so a moderator can reach these controller actions directly (the route constraint only applies to route recognition; if the controller is reachable the before_filter is the only guard, and `ensure_staff` passes for moderators). Every other admin resource controller in this codebase relies on AdminConstraint at the route level and does not add `ensure_staff`. Either drop the before_filter (route constraint is sufficient and stricter) or change it to `ensure_admin` for defense in depth. As written, moderators can create/update/destroy embeddable hosts, which is an admin-only settings change.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.import silently falls back to no category when the embed URL's host is not registered
findings.body: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` returns `false` (not nil) when the host is not found or the URI is invalid (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11-12). The code then does `category: eh.try(:category_id)` — `false.try(:category_id)` returns nil, so PostCreator receives `category: nil`. Previously the category came from `SiteSetting.embed_category`, which had a configured default. Now, any import whose URL host has no EmbeddableHost row (e.g. a feed item from a newly added feed URL, or a host row deleted by an admin) creates a topic with no category, which lands in uncategorized (or fails validation if `allow_uncategorized_topics` is false and the user is not staff). This is a silent behavior change for the RSS/feed polling path (Jobs::PollFeed → TopicEmbed.import). The import should either skip/flag such URLs or fall back to a configured default category.

findings.title: update action is a no-op that just re-renders show
findings.body: `update` simply re-renders the embedding serializer without reading or applying any params. The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` (config/routes.rb:139) and the client controller's `saveChanges` action (`this.get('embedding').update({})` in admin-embedding.js.es6:6) imply that settings can be saved through this endpoint, but nothing is persisted — the OpenStruct built in `fetch_embedding` is rebuilt from the DB on every request and no attributes are ever assigned. Either implement actual update semantics (e.g. accept and persist embedding-level settings) or remove the PUT route and the `saveChanges` action so the UI does not imply a save that silently does nothing.

findings.title: Controller specs only assert inheritance; no coverage of create/update/destroy, authorization, or validation
findings.body: Both new controller specs (this file and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) contain a single test asserting the controller is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. There are no tests that: a non-admin/non-staff user is rejected; an admin can create a host with a valid host+category; invalid hosts are rejected with a 422; updating a nonexistent id returns an error rather than 500 (see the nil-host bug in the controller); destroying a host works. Given that the controller has real logic (save_host, nil-record handling, category fallback), the specs should exercise the HTTP endpoints with `sign_in(Fabricate(:admin))` etc.

findings.title: Model spec does not test nil host, duplicate hosts, or invalid formats
findings.body: The spec covers http/https/path trimming and host_allowed? lookups, but does not test: (1) `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil)` — which currently crashes in before_validation (nil.sub!), so a regression there would not be caught; (2) duplicate hosts — there is no uniqueness validation and no test pinning down the desired behavior; (3) invalid formats (e.g. `host` with spaces, `http://`, uppercase, port-only) to confirm the regex rejects them. Adding these would lock in the intended contract.

findings.title: Template renders nothing (not even the Add Host button) when there are no hosts, due to {{#if}} wrapping only the table
findings.body: The `{{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` block wraps only the table; the `{{d-button ... action="addHost"}}` at line 14 is outside it, so the button does render. However, when the serializer uses `embed: :ids` (see the EmbeddingSerializer finding), `embedding.embeddable_hosts` will be an empty/undefined array on first load, so the table is hidden — which is correct — but combined with the hydration bug the page will appear permanently empty with no way to tell the admin why. More importantly, there is no empty-state message; a fresh install shows only an 'Add Host' button with no explanation. Minor UX issue, but the empty table header (Host / Post to Category) is also hidden, so the user gets no column context. Consider an explicit empty-state row.

findings.title: expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable host exists, changing behavior for sites with no hosts configured
findings.body: The method changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The old check ensured the expand-embed UI was only offered when the site actually had embed hosts configured. The new version returns true for any topic that has a TopicEmbed row, regardless of whether any EmbeddableHost exists. The spec at spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1403 ('is false if embeddable_host is blank') now passes only because no host is fabricated in that example — but the method itself no longer consults the hosts table at all, so the test name is misleading and the guard is gone. If the intent was to drop the setting check because hosts are now per-embed, the method should instead verify the topic's embed URL host is registered (e.g. via `TopicEmbed` + `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`), otherwise the 'expand embed' affordance can appear on sites that have disabled embedding entirely (all hosts deleted).

findings.title: embeddable_hosts resource routes are not scoped under /customize, producing a top-level /admin/embeddable_hosts REST API
findings.body: `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` is declared at the admin namespace root (line 153), so it generates `/admin/embeddable_hosts` (index/create) and `/admin/embeddable_hosts/:id` (show/update/destroy). The Ember adapter for `embeddable-host` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6 is for the embedding model; the host model uses the default rest adapter with ADMIN_MODELS prefix `/admin/`) will call `/admin/embeddable_hosts` — consistent. But this exposes a full REST resource (including index and show, which the controller does not define — those will 404/raise AbstractController::ActionNotFound) at a top-level admin path, unlike sibling resources (site_texts, user_fields, emojis) which are scoped under `/customize`. The controller only implements create/update/destroy; index/show are missing. Either scope the resource (`scope "/customize" do resources :embeddable_hosts ... end`) to match siblings, or restrict with `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]`.
